study: O'Hare et al. 2019 (FFT Literacy Reciprocal Reading, EEF efficacy trial; QUB CESI evaluation)
eval_evidence: EEF-commissioned independent evaluation by the Centre for Evidence and Social Innovation, Queen's University Belfast (O'Hare et al.); the developer (FFT Literacy) delivered the programme while QUB independently evaluated it -- standard EEF independent-evaluator model.
developer_evidence: Reciprocal Reading is FFT Literacy's programme; the developer (FFT) trained and supported the participating teachers to deliver it (developer-led efficacy trial). QUB only evaluated.
cascade_evidence: FFT (the developer) trained the schools'/teachers' delivery directly in this efficacy trial; no train-the-trainer intermediary documented. (Note: design/extraction record does not detail an extra cascade hop.)
counterfactual_evidence: Cluster RCT with business-as-usual control (49 control schools continued normal reading provision); extraction record and EEF report state BAU comparison.
coaching_evidence: Programme is teacher training in the Reciprocal Reading approach (initial training + materials/support) delivered by FFT; no ongoing in-class coaching cycles described in the extraction record/report for the universal arm.
student_dose_evidence: Universal arm (the registry-matched 'All' population, Year 4): whole-class teaching changes only -- the teacher's own reading instruction. (Targeted arm uses small-group pull-out for pre-selected poor comprehenders, but that arm is the non-full-sample secondary contrast; the registry row maps to the universal whole-class arm.)
maturity_evidence: One-academic-year intervention; outcomes measured immediately post (~1 year). EEF efficacy trial designed as a single year; no maturity wave.
